title: Confidence Curve Retro & Task Decomposition
content:
Week: 2026-03-08 → 2026-03-12
Owner: Amir Desai (solo notes + quick sync followups)
Context: personal retro focused on confidence vs actual delivery and how I broke down tasks for the KV-cache + batching spike. Trying to converge on a reliable decomposition pattern for medium-sized infra spikes.

Topline metrics (personal instrumentation):
- Planned story points: 8 (decomposed into 5 tasks)
- Completed story points: 5
- Unblocked days lost: 2 (blocked by infra quota, test infra flakiness)
- Confidence delta (start -> end): 0.6 -> 0.4 (confidence dropped after integration)
- Time spent debugging infra vs dev: ~60/40

What I tried this week (short):
1) Task decomposition pattern: "probe -> verify -> harden"
   - Probe: small prototype in feature branch to measure latency of KV cache lookups
   - Verify: integration test with synthetic load (local harness + limited GPU)
   - Harden: add fallback & telemetry hooks for edge cases
2) Parallel micro-experiments: two concurrent approaches to batching window (50ms vs 150ms)
3) Quick canary in staging on dedicated pool (Sophie helped run smoke)

Surface observations (raw):
- Decomposition was ok for the first half, but I underestimated integration complexity with the routing layer. The probe uncovered an incompatibility that required refactor (cost 1 full day).
- Confidence scoring is too subjective — need a tiny rubric (see below)
- Batching window 50ms gave better 99p latency under light load but throughput drop under bursty patterns; 150ms smoothed latency but increased p50 when load low.
- Test infra flakiness is eating momentum — need a short experiment to make deterministic synthetic loads (Ravi to help with harness).

Mini-rubric for confidence (proposal):
- 0.0 - 0.3: only prototypes, no integration tests.
- 0.31 - 0.6: unit + component tests, limited stg smoke.
- 0.61 - 0.8: end-to-end in staging, perf baselines measured.
- 0.81 - 1.0: green canary + performance regression guardrails.

Hypotheses and experiments (next sprint):
- H1: If we use a dynamic batching window that adapts to short-term request cadence (micro-bursts), we can keep p99 under target while improving throughput. Experiment: implement a simple EWMA of inter-arrival and switch windows; measure for 72h in staging. (Linked: ENG-4821)
- H2: Adding a lightweight integration shim in routing reduces integration defects by ~50% because we can test compatibility earlier. Experiment: add shim + run compatibility test matrix in CI.

Open questions / unresolved:
- How to measure "integration complexity" early? (proposed proxy: number of distinct cross-service calls added during probe)
- What safety rollback thresholds should we set for dynamic batching? (p99 latency > baseline + 30%?)
- Do we need a dedicated flaky-test quarantine in CI to reduce noise?

Concrete next actions (me + collaborators):
- Amir: implement EWMA-based adaptive window prototype (spike, 2d).
- Sophie: run the staging canary on dedicated pool and capture memory/latency traces (end of sprint).
- Ravi: stabilize synthetic load harness and add deterministic scenarios (blocker removal).
- All: quick doc outlining the confidence rubric and share in #eng-serving-runtime by Fri.

Short retrospective notes (tone: candid):
- What went well: quick prototyping loop, visibility into latency tradeoffs, teammates responsive for canary runs.
- What went poorly: underestimated integration churn, too many context switches (meetings), test infra noise.
- One small change that'll help: adopt a 30-minute daily sync block for deep work during spikes — remove meeting collisions.

Quick timeline sketch:
- Mon/Tue next sprint: spike (EWMA prototype) + small refactor to decouple routing (1.5d)
- Wed: run deterministic load (Ravi), analyze results (0.5d)
- Thu: staging canary (Sophie) + collect traces (0.5d)
- Fri: synthesize results, update confidence rubric, decision: roll forward vs rollback plan.

Notes to self (fragile bits / talk track for manager check-in):
- Emphasize that this is an architecture-level tradeoff: latency epsilon vs throughput smoothing. Need manager buy-in for a short on-call experiment window to safely test in dedicated pool.
- Call out test infra flakiness as impediment to predictability — propose small funding for a 2-week SRE-funded harness cleanup.

Random ideas / brainstorm (one-liners):
- Add a tiny "gamma day" each sprint where we only unblock infra issues (no new features). Might reduce context-switch overhead.
- Create a lightweight "integration checklist" that must be filled after probe stage before verify begins.
- Measure developer-level confidence and correlate with number of unknown cross-service interactions.

Slack refs: #eng-serving-runtime (thread: "kv-batching-canary"), pinned message id: 16283902 (see linked artifacts)
GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1987 (proto + perf harness)
Jira: ENG-4821 (adaptive-batching-experiment)
Confluence: kv-cache-batching-hypotheses (doc id in linked_artifacts)

End of note.
